title: `autoOfflineActive` is not published, so every offline indicator in the app renders a stale value
claim: `autoOfflineActive` is a plain stored `private var` and `effectiveOfflineMode` is computed from it, so flipping the flag publishes nothing. The entry asserts every reader — the Settings 'Active' subtitle, the 'Browsing downloaded content only' label, `RadioTabView.canLoadDirectory`, Discovery's search gates — keeps rendering the old value, and that in `.homeWifi` mode walking onto another network 'produces no publish at all'.
no_video_reason: The headline symptom did not occur, so there is no defect to film for it; the surviving defect is a signed-out user flipping auto-offline, whose missing re-render cannot be distinguished on screen from ordinary Radio loading without instrumenting the app, which this run may not do.

surviving_defect.title: `autoOfflineActive` is unpublished, so correctness depends on an unrelated incidental publish — and a signed-out user gets none
surviving_defect.description: `private var autoOfflineActive` (AppModel.swift:726) carries no @Published. Readers re-render today only because `applyEffectiveOfflinePresentation()` happens to trigger an unguarded @Published write to `serverConnectionHealth` — and that call is gated on `hasInternetPath, isSignedIn`. A signed-out user, for whom Radio's directory is explicitly usable (`canLoadDirectory` has no sign-in check), gets no invalidation when auto-offline flips.
surviving_defect.proposed_fix: `@Published private(set) var autoOfflineActive = false`, assigned through an equality guard (`let next = ...; if next != autoOfflineActive { autoOfflineActive = next }`) matching the file's existing pattern for `hasInternetPath`. No view changes.

description: A claim that the app's offline indicators would show out-of-date information because the underlying flag does not notify the interface when it changes.
issue: As written, nothing goes wrong for a signed-in user on a network. The stale-render symptom the entry describes does not occur, because the flag is always set before a publish that follows it. A genuine but much narrower defect does survive: the correct behaviour is accidental rather than designed, and one specific case — a signed-out user — gets no publish at all.
proposed_fix: No fix for the headline as written (the stated stale render does not occur). Apply the two-line robustness fix in surviving_defect.
steps: Read the entry's claim and both review passes, which contradict each other on publish ordering.

Locate the symbols by name rather than by the cited line numbers, which have drifted: AppModel.swift has absorbed several post-sweep commits, moving these ~265 lines from the cited 711-712 / 6135-6157.

Confirm at AppModel.swift:725-726 that `var effectiveOfflineMode: Bool { offlineMode || autoOfflineActive }` is computed and `private var autoOfflineActive = false` carries no `@Published` — so the flag itself publishes nothing. This half of the claim is TRUE.

Read `evaluateAutoOfflineMode()` in full: on the guard path and on both `.wifiOnly` and `.homeWifi` branches, `autoOfflineActive` is assigned BEFORE the trailing `applyEffectiveOfflinePresentation()` call. There is no branch where the flag is set after.

Read `applyEffectiveOfflinePresentation()`: its body is `if hasInternetPath, isSignedIn { Task { await refreshServerConnectionHealth() } }`, and `refreshServerConnectionHealth` assigns the `@Published private(set) var serverConnectionHealth` (declared AppModel.swift:213) with no equality guard — so it publishes on every call.
Conclude the stated symptom does not reproduce for a signed-in user on a network: the flag is already updated when the publish lands.

Test the `.homeWifi` sub-claim specifically: that branch is only reached when `hasInternetPath` is true, which is the very gate on the publish — so 'produces no publish at all' is directly contradicted by the source.

Identify what does survive: the publish is gated on `isSignedIn`, and Radio's directory is usable signed out (`canLoadDirectory` has no sign-in check), so a signed-out user flipping auto-offline gets no invalidation.
notes: WHERE REALITY DIVERGES FROM THE DOCUMENT: the mechanism is correct (the flag is unpublished) but the stated impact is not. Every named reader re-renders correctly for a signed-in, connected user, because evaluateAutoOfflineMode sets the flag before applyEffectiveOfflinePresentation() triggers an unguarded @Published write to serverConnectionHealth. The .homeWifi 'no publish at all' sub-claim is false on its face, since that branch requires hasInternetPath. not_reproduced rather than already_fixed because NO commit fixed this — the code still matches the sweep; its reasoning about consequences was wrong from the start. Filed DENIED by the sweep; the T238 re-verification (agent 03) records `Denial: DOES NOT HOLD`, `Problem: PARTLY REAL` — this run agrees: headline wrong, narrow defect real, carried in surviving_defect so it arrives as its own card.
